title: A system's level of agency must be determined empirically by prediction and control

fields.label: Label
fields.value: A system's level of agency must be determined empirically by prediction and control

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Under TAME, how much agency a system has is an empirical, observer-dependent question: the correct level of agency to attribute is the one whose model and intervention strategy give the most efficient prediction and control of the system, as established by experiment.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Philosophical Foundations of an Approach to Diverse Intelligences

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Thus, the correct level of agency with which to treat any system must be determined by experiments that reveal which kind of model and strategy provides the most efficient predictive and control capability over the system.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Philosophical Foundations of an Approach to Diverse Intelligences”. Scope: Any living, engineered or hybrid system

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-05: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.53

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The pragmatic criterion can be benchmarked for particular systems after defining efficiency. Existing datasets permit examples, but the framework's observer and task dependence prevents a single general empirical resolution.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For a specified system and task, compare models at different attributed agency levels using held-out predictive accuracy, control success, intervention cost, and model complexity; the preferred level minimizes a prespecified combined cost.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Results are task-specific and cannot establish a universal correct agency level.

Efficiency combines accuracy, control, complexity, and cost in observer-dependent ways.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.52
data adequacy: 0.35
data existence: 0.52
operationalizability: 0.68
analysis feasibility: 0.58

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The statement is a rule for attributing agency: use whichever model gives the most efficient prediction and control. Experiments can rank models, and the ranking cannot come out against the rule, because the rule defines the preferred level as the winner. That is a methodological stipulation rather than a result public data could refute.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Model comparison can rank which description predicts and controls a system most efficiently, and under this claim the winner is the correct agency level by definition.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: Every outcome of a predictive comparison is compatible with the claim, because the claim stipulates that the best-controlling model is the right level of agency.
